_about: A PLACE HAS TRAITS (rule 71, Paolo 10/4: 'settlements have traits too, depending on random variables'). Battle Brothers' settlement situations, in our skin. RUN TWO rolls them from this file per place (seeded by the place's name and the week, so a trait comes and goes); each one changes the PICTURE (look), the SHOPS' prices and stock, WHO stands at the posts, and what the KEEPERS say. Numbers are Battle Brothers-shaped and marked for TUNING; words are draft:true. COMBAT TWO draws the real picture variants later (burnt, boarded, flooded, market day): when a 'variant' name is set here and that picture exists, it is drawn instead of the overlay.

says.any: A crew came through three nights back. Burned the Ortega house. Everything costs more now, mijo.
says.hall: Nobody wants work. They want to leave.
says.smith: Everybody wants a blade fixed since the raid. I am three deep already.
says.armourer: Half my stock walked out the door with the crew that hit us. What is left costs more.
says.barber: Nobody wants a new face right now. They want their old one back.
says.clinic: Three of mine from the raid are still on the cots. I am not taking anyone new today.
says.board: Nobody wants to leave the block long enough to work a job, not since the raid.

says.any: Half the block is coughing. They boarded up the clinic windows to keep it in.
says.hall: Nobody is signing on. Not with the cough going around.
says.smith: Keep your hands off my tools if you have been near the clinic.
says.armourer: I am not touching a man's armour until the cough clears. Bad luck, same as bad metal.
says.barber: No cuts while the cough is going around. I am not catching it off your collar.
says.clinic: Half the block is on my cots already. I have no room for anything new.
says.board: Nobody wants a job that takes them near the sick houses. I do not blame them.

says.any: Market day. Everybody is out, everything is moving, prices are down.
says.hall: Lot of new faces in town today. Some of them want work.
says.smith: Everybody wants a blade sharp for market day. Busy, but good busy.
says.armourer: Sold three pieces before noon. Market day does that.
says.barber: Everybody wants to look good for market day. Sit, sit, there is a line.
says.clinic: Quiet today. Even the sick ones are out at the market.
says.board: New faces in town for market day. A few of them want work.
